web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: Is NKE building a Stage 1 base after its 45% drawdown, or is it still trapped under declining 30-week and 200-day moving averages with no short-term momentum edge?

epigraph.quote: Never try to catch a falling knife—wait for the blade to stick in the floor, stop vibrating, and prove that institutional buyers are willing to lift it above its 30-week moving average on expanding volume.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, NKE closed at $37.99 (+0.61% daily; -1.55% 1-week; +2.29% 1-month; -2.81% 3-month per our TradingView session ledger) [23, 29]. Its technical posture sits in Stage 1 (Basing): price has stabilized +2.98% above its 50-day SMA ($36.89) and +0.53% above its 10-week EMA ($37.79) off the $31.97 low [29]. However, higher-timeframe resistance remains heavy because shares sit -6.82% below a falling 30-week SMA ($40.77) and -15.18% below a falling 200-day SMA ($44.79) [29]. Both `stock_snapshot.py` and `options_snapshot.py` enforce CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (`WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_RETEST`) [29].

web_blocks.takeaway: NKE has stabilized above its 50-day SMA ($36.89) after a +2.29% 1-month bounce, but remains trapped beneath declining 30-week ($40.77) and 200-day ($44.79) ceilings.

web_blocks.title: Institutional Ownership, Short Interest & Insider Form 4 Conviction

web_blocks.html: Positioning shows a tug-of-war between insiders and short sellers. Institutional ownership is 68.79% (+0.94% recent change), while short interest reached 92.92 million shares, or 7.91% of float (2.83 days to cover) [23]. Friday's volume (12.18M shares) ran at 0.54x its 20-day average (and 0.37x its 3-month Finviz average) [23, 29]. Quiet volume on a bounce signals no institutional accumulation yet.

On the insider side, SEC Form 4 filings show CEO Elliott Hill invested roughly $2.0 million in open-market buys [30, 31]. He bought 16,388 shares at ~$61.10 ($1.0M) in December 2025, and 23,660 shares at ~$42.27 ($1.0M) in April 2026 alongside directors Tim Cook and Robert Swan [30]. Insider buying confirms management conviction, but shares still trade ~10% below Hill's April buy [23, 30].

web_blocks.title: Market Regime Context & Options / Momentum Edge Assessment

web_blocks.html: Broad market conditions reinforce patience. As of November 13, 2026, the US market sits in a Correction regime (S&P 500 below its 50-DMA, 52.6% breadth above 50-DMA, and 6 distribution days over 25 sessions) [29]. Buying a sub-200-DMA stock in a Correction fights both stock and market trends.

Options pricing also favors waiting. NKE's 30-day ATM implied volatility is 44.3% versus 20-day realized volatility of 35.0% (`IV_ELEVATED`) ahead of December 17 earnings [24, 29]. Because IV carries a +9.3 point premium and `intraday_4h_turn` is false, buying naked calls at $37.99 has negative edge [29]. Note also that the scanner's illustrative `2027-01-15` $37.5/$42.5 call spread (61 DTE) expires just ~29 days after December 17 earnings; any conditional options entry at the $34.02 shelf should either wait until after earnings or use a longer-dated March/June 2027 expiry [29].

A valid Stage 2 breakout requires three steps. First, price must hold a higher low above $34.02 on light selling volume. Second, weekly closes must reclaim the 30-week SMA ($40.77) and Pivot R1 ($41.28) on >= 1.5x weekly volume [29]. Third, the 200-day SMA ($44.79) must flatten as Q2/Q3 FY2027 results confirm margin repair [23, 24].

Overhead supply mapping explains why prior bounces stalled. Between $40.77 and $44.79, the 30-week SMA, Pivot R2 ($43.89), 200-day SMA, and Hill's $42.27 buy zone all converge [29, 30]. Clearing that $41–$45 wall demands a real fundamental catalyst on December 17, not 0.37x-volume drift [23, 24].

Relative strength versus both the S&P 500 and footwear peers confirms the lack of leadership. Over the past 3 months, NKE fell -2.81% while failing to hold above its 30-week average [29]. Meanwhile, active Stage 2 leaders across the US market trade above rising 10-week and 30-week averages on expanding volume. In Stan Weinstein's discipline, capital belongs in confirmed Stage 2 leaders or cash—never trapped in a Stage 1 basing zone under a falling 200-day ceiling.

Downside support levels are equally clear on the weekly chart. First support sits at the 50-day SMA ($36.89), followed by the primary Pivot S1 shelf at $34.02 and the 52-week cycle low at $31.97 [29]. A high-volume undercut of $34.02 that quickly reclaims $34.50–$35.00 would create the first asymmetric swing setup. Conversely, a weekly close below $31.50 breaks the entire base and opens air down toward Pivot S2 ($29.36) [29].

book_paragraphs: Now let's pull up the price chart and read what institutional money is actually doing with its feet. At Friday's close of $37.99, NIKE is sitting in a Stage 1 basing zone. Over the past month, the stock nudged up 2.29% (down 1.55% on the week and 2.81% over three months) to climb +2.98% above its 50-day simple moving average at $36.89 and +0.53% above its 10-week EMA at $37.79.

But zoom out to the weekly and 200-day charts, and the overhead supply is unmistakable. NIKE's 30-week moving average sits at $40.77 and is still sloping downward. Its 200-day moving average sits way up at $44.79—more than 15% above the current price. In Stan Weinstein's framework, a stock trading 15% below a falling 200-day moving average has not earned a Stage 2 breakout. Every rally into the $40.77 to $44.79 zone runs straight into trapped shareholders looking to sell at breakeven.

Notice the volume and positioning clues too. On November 13, NKE traded just 12.18 million shares—0.54x its 20-day average (0.37x its 3-month average). True institutional accumulation announces itself with 1.5x to 2.5x volume surges on up-weeks, not quiet 0.54x drift. Meanwhile, short interest stands at 92.9 million shares, or 7.91% of the float. Bears are still leaning on the tape.

Yes, CEO Elliott Hill put $2.0 million of his own cash into open-market purchases—$1.0 million at $61.10 in December 2025 and another $1.0 million at $42.27 in April 2026 alongside Tim Cook and Robert Swan. I respect insiders writing real checks. But insider buying tells you what management believes three years from now; it does not override a falling 30-week moving average or a broader US market sitting in a Correction with six distribution days. Short-term momentum edge right here? Zero. We either wait for a washout retest of the $33.50–$35.00 support shelf, or we wait for NKE to prove itself by reclaiming $40.77–$44.79 on heavy volume.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Insider buying at $61 and $42 proves management's conviction, not the timing of the bottom. When a stock trades 15% below its 200-day moving average in a Correction regime, patience is a position.

book_subsections.title: Why Elevated Implied Volatility Punishes Impatient Call Buyers
paragraphs: Walk through the options pricing for a moment, because it reinforces the exact same discipline. With Q2 FY2027 earnings expected around December 17, 2026, NIKE's at-the-money implied volatility is 44.3% compared to 20-day realized volatility of 35.0%. Option sellers are already charging a 9.3-point volatility premium.

If you buy outright shares or naked calls at $37.99 today, you are paying elevated volatility in a stock with neutral daily RSI (50.23) and weak weekly RSI (40.46). If NKE drifts sideways or tests its $34.02 pivot shelf before earnings, time decay and IV compression eat your capital. That is why our technical gate says: stand aside at $37.99, and act only at confirmed support ($33.50–$35.00) or on a Stage 2 volume breakout.

book_subsections.title: Reading Overhead Supply: The $40.77 to $44.79 Gauntlet
paragraphs: When you and I study a weekly chart after a 45% decline, we always ask: where are the trapped buyers sitting? For NIKE, the heaviest overhead supply band sits right between $40.77 and $44.79—spanning the declining 30-week moving average, Pivot R1 at $41.28, Pivot R2 at $43.89, and the 200-day moving average at $44.79. Notice that even CEO Elliott Hill's April 2026 open-market purchase at $42.27 sits smack in the middle of that ceiling.

Until institutional volume surges to 1.5x or 2.0x normal weekly turnover and drives price decisively above $44.79, every bounce from $37.99 toward $41 faces natural selling pressure. Respecting that overhead gauntlet is what separates disciplined Stage 2 trend followers from investors who tie up capital for quarters in dead-money range trade.

book_subsections.title: Aligning Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Timeframes
paragraphs: Notice how our three timeframes tell a coherent story when you stack them together. On the 4-hour chart, NKE is drifting just below its 20-period EMA ($38.49) and right on its 50-period SMA ($37.90) with a 4H RSI of 46.11—no intraday turn signal has fired yet. On the daily chart, price sits modestly above the 50-day SMA ($36.89) with a neutral RSI of 50.23, reflecting a modest one-month relief bounce off the lows.

On the weekly chart, however, the primary trend remains decisively down: weekly RSI is 40.46, price sits nearly 7% below the 30-week moving average ($40.77), and Friday's volume ran at just 0.54x its 20-day average. True bottoming formations require all three timeframes to stop fighting each other—either by washing down into the $34.02 Pivot S1 shelf where buyers step in aggressively, or by building a tight multi-week Volatility Contraction Pattern just beneath $40.77 before breaking out on institutional volume.
